recipes.title: Kappa Puzhukku (Mashed Tapioca with Coconut)
recipes.description: Boiled tapioca mashed with a crushed coconut, shallot, garlic and green chilli mix and tempered in coconut oil. Starchy and hearty — traditionally eaten with fish curry, so keep the portion modest.

steps.title: Peel the tapioca
steps.text: Cut the tapioca into 4-inch lengths, slit the thick bark and peel it off with the pink inner skin. Remove the woody central fibre and cut into 1½-inch pieces. Wash well.
steps.visual: Peeled white tapioca pieces in a bowl of water, curls of brown and pink peel on the board beside

steps.title: Boil and drain
steps.text: Boil the tapioca in the water for 10 minutes, then drain and discard the water. Add fresh water to cover with the turmeric and salt and cook another 10 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
steps.visual: Soft, yellow-tinged tapioca pieces in a colander, steam rising

steps.title: Crush the coconut mix
steps.text: Pulse the coconut, shallots, garlic, green chillies and cumin in a mixer without water to a coarse crumble.
steps.visual: Coarse, moist coconut crumble with green chilli and shallot bits in a mixer jar

steps.title: Mash with coconut
steps.text: Return the tapioca to the pan, add the coconut mix and mash roughly with a spoon over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes so the coconut cooks and everything comes together.
steps.visual: Roughly mashed yellow tapioca mixed with white coconut crumble in the saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small pan, splutter mustard seeds, add the dried red chillies and curry leaves and pour over the puzhukku. Mix well.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, red chillies and curry leaves in sizzling coconut oil being poured over the mashed tapioca

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with mathi curry, fish fry or chammanthi. Treat it as the starch of the meal — about one cup — rather than eating it alongside rice.
steps.visual: A mound of yellow kappa puzhukku on a banana leaf flecked with coconut and curry leaves, beside a clay pot of red sardine curry

substitutions.note: Chena (yam) puzhukku is made the same way and is a little lower in carbs.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a pan with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.title: Matta Kanji and Payar (Red Rice Gruel with Green Moong)
recipes.description: Kerala's homely one-bowl meal: soft matta rice kanji eaten with green moong tossed with coconut, shallots and green chilli. Light on the stomach and very filling.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Soak the green moong for 4 hours. Wash the matta rice and soak it for 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Two steel bowls, one with soaked green moong and one with reddish matta rice in water

steps.title: Cook the kanji
steps.text: Pressure cook the rice with 5 cups of the water and a pinch of salt for 6 to 7 whistles, about 25 minutes, then simmer open for a few minutes until the grains are very soft and the kanji is thick but flowing. In a pot, simmer for 45 minutes.
steps.visual: Soft, swollen red rice grains in thick white kanji water in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Cook the moong
steps.text: Cook the soaked moong in 1 cup of the water with a pinch of salt for 10 to 12 minutes in a saucepan until soft but whole. Drain any extra water into the kanji.
steps.visual: Soft whole green moong in a small saucepan, almost dry

steps.title: Season the payar
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai, splutter mustard seeds, add curry leaves, shallots, garlic and green chilli and sauté for 2 minutes. Add the moong and coconut and toss for 2 minutes until dry.
steps.visual: Green moong tossed with grated coconut, shallots and curry leaves in a black kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle the hot kanji into bowls, add salt to taste and serve the payar on the side. Add a spoon of chammanthi or a pickle if you like.
steps.visual: A deep bowl of steaming red-rice kanji beside a small mound of green moong payar with coconut, served with a ladle on a banana leaf

substitutions.note: Brown rice is the closest swap if matta rice isn't available.

recipes.storage: Kanji thickens as it stands; refrigerate for up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Thin with hot water and bring to a boil.

recipes.title: Pavakka Theeyal (Bitter Gourd in Roasted Coconut Gravy)
recipes.description: Bitter gourd and shallots simmered in a dark, tangy tamarind gravy thickened with coconut roasted with coriander and dried chillies until almost black, balanced with a touch of jaggery.

steps.title: Prepare the bitter gourd
steps.text: Slice the bitter gourd into thin rounds and remove the seeds. Rub with a little salt and leave 10 minutes, then squeeze out the juice to reduce bitterness. Soak the tamarind.
steps.visual: Thin green bitter gourd rounds in a bowl, salted and releasing juice, tamarind soaking in a cup beside

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: In a dry kadai on medium-low heat, roast the coconut with the coriander seeds, dried red chillies and fenugreek, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes until the coconut is a very dark, even brown and the oil starts to show. Don't let it burn.
steps.visual: Very dark brown roasted coconut with coriander seeds and red chillies in a black kadai, glistening with its own oil

steps.title: Grind to a paste
steps.text: Cool, add the turmeric and grind with ½ cup water to a very smooth, almost black paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, nearly black coconut paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the vegetables
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of the coconut oil in the kadai and fry the bitter gourd and shallots on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the gourd is browned at the edges.
steps.visual: Browned bitter gourd rounds and golden halved shallots frying in coconut oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer in tamarind
steps.text: Strain in the tamarind water, add the water, salt and jaggery and boil for 5 minutes. Stir in the roasted paste and simmer on low for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and dark.
steps.visual: Bitter gourd and shallots in a thick, dark brown gravy bubbling in the kadai, oil rising to the top

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining coconut oil, splutter the mustard seeds, add curry leaves and pour over the theeyal.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds and curry leaves crackling in coconut oil poised over the dark theeyal

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for at least 30 minutes — theeyal tastes better as it sits. Serve with rice and a mild thoran or moru curry.
steps.visual: Dark brown pavakka theeyal in a clay bowl with bitter gourd rounds, shallots and curry leaves, rice beside it on a banana leaf

substitutions.note: Leave out the jaggery for a sharper, sugar-free theeyal.
Drumstick or brinjal theeyal is made the same way.

recipes.reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Ulli Theeyal (Shallots in Roasted Coconut–Tamarind Gravy)
recipes.description: Whole shallots and garlic cooked in a tangy tamarind gravy darkened with deeply roasted coconut, coriander and chilli — Kerala's most beloved theeyal.

steps.title: Peel the shallots
steps.text: Peel the shallots and garlic, leaving them whole. Soak the tamarind in warm water.
steps.visual: A heap of peeled whole pink shallots and garlic cloves on a board, tamarind soaking in a cup

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: Dry roast the coconut, coriander seeds, dried red chillies and fenugreek in a kadai on medium-low heat for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring constantly, until dark brown and fragrant.
steps.visual: Dark brown roasted coconut with coriander seeds and red chillies in a black kadai

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Cool, add the turmeric and grind with ½ cup water to a smooth, dark paste.
steps.visual: Smooth dark brown roasted coconut paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Sauté the shallots
steps.text: Heat 2 teaspoons of the coconut oil in the kadai and sauté the whole shallots and garlic on medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and slightly soft.
steps.visual: Golden whole shallots and garlic cloves sautéing in coconut oil in the black kadai

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Strain in the tamarind water, add the water and salt and simmer for 6 minutes until the shallots are tender. Add the roasted paste and simmer on low for 8 to 10 minutes until thick, dark and glossy.
steps.visual: Whole shallots in a thick, dark brown, glossy gravy simmering in the kadai

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the remaining coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, add curry leaves and pour over the theeyal.
steps.visual: Crackling mustard seeds and curry leaves in coconut oil being poured over the shallot theeyal

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for 30 minutes and serve with rice, a thoran and pappadam.
steps.visual: Ulli theeyal in a clay pot, glossy whole shallots in dark gravy with curry leaves, matta rice beside it

substitutions.note: Quartered small onions work if shallots are hard to find.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; flavour improves overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Achinga Payar Mezhukkupuratti (Long Bean Stir-Fry)
recipes.description: Long beans cut into short pieces and stir-fried in coconut oil with crushed shallots, garlic and red chilli flakes until blistered — the simplest Kerala side.

steps.title: Cut the beans
steps.text: Wash the long beans and cut them into 1-inch pieces. Crush the shallots and garlic coarsely with the chilli flakes in a mortar.
steps.visual: Short pieces of long beans on a board beside a stone mortar with coarsely crushed shallots, garlic and red chilli flakes

steps.title: Steam the beans
steps.text: Put the beans in a kadai with turmeric, salt and the water. Cover and cook on medium heat for 5 minutes until just tender.
steps.visual: Green long bean pieces steaming under a lid in a black kadai

steps.title: Add the crushed mix
steps.text: Push the beans aside, add the coconut oil to the centre and fry the crushed shallot mixture and curry leaves for 1 minute.
steps.visual: Crushed shallot, garlic and chilli flakes sizzling in a pool of coconut oil in the middle of the beans in the kadai

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Toss everything together and stir-fry on medium-high heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the beans are blistered in spots and coated.
steps.visual: Blistered long beans coated in red chilli flakes and fried shallots in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with rice and moru curry, or as a side with chicken curry.
steps.visual: Achinga payar mezhukkupuratti heaped on a banana leaf, green beans flecked with red chilli and curry leaves

substitutions.note: Crush dried red chillies yourself for a fresher flavour.
French beans work the same way.

recipes.reheating: Warm in a hot pan for 1 minute.

recipes.title: Kovakka Mezhukkupuratti (Ivy Gourd Stir-Fry with Coconut Slivers)
recipes.description: Ivy gourd slices roasted in coconut oil with shallots, garlic, chilli, pepper and thin coconut slivers until crisp-edged and caramelised.

steps.title: Slice the kovakka
steps.text: Trim the ivy gourd and cut each lengthwise into 4 thin wedges. Toss with turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
steps.visual: Thin green ivy gourd wedges tossed with red chilli and turmeric in a steel bowl

steps.title: Fry the coconut
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai, splutter mustard seeds, then fry the coconut slivers and curry leaves on medium-low heat for 2 minutes until golden.
steps.visual: Golden coconut slivers, mustard seeds and curry leaves frying in coconut oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Add shallots
steps.text: Add the shallots and garlic and sauté for 2 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Sliced shallots and garlic softening with coconut slivers in the kadai

steps.title: Roast the kovakka
steps.text: Add the ivy gourd and stir-fry uncovered on medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until tender with browned, slightly crisp edges.
steps.visual: Ivy gourd wedges browned and caramelised at the edges with coconut slivers in the kadai

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle the crushed pepper, toss and serve hot with rice and sambar or moru curry.
steps.visual: Kovakka mezhukkupuratti in a steel bowl, browned green wedges with golden coconut slivers, curry leaves and pepper

substitutions.note: Skip the coconut slivers for a lighter stir-fry.

recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in a hot pan for 2 minutes.

recipes.title: Thenga Chammanthi (Roasted Chilli Coconut Chutney)
recipes.description: A coarse, dry Kerala coconut chutney ground with fire-roasted red chillies, shallots, ginger and a little tamarind, finished with a drizzle of raw coconut oil.

steps.title: Roast the chillies
steps.text: Roast the dried red chillies on a dry tawa over low heat for 1 to 2 minutes, turning, until they darken and smell smoky. Add the shallots and curry leaves for the last minute.
steps.visual: Darkened dried red chillies, shallots and curry leaves roasting on a black iron tawa

steps.title: Grind coarsely
steps.text: Pulse the roasted chillies with the coconut, shallots, ginger, tamarind and salt in a mixer without water, in short bursts, until it is a coarse, slightly moist crumble that holds when pressed.
steps.visual: Coarse, pale orange-red coconut crumble flecked with chilli in an open mixer jar

steps.title: Shape and finish
steps.text: Press the chammanthi into a ball or a mound with your hands and drizzle the raw coconut oil over.
steps.visual: A firm orange-red ball of coconut chammanthi glistening with coconut oil on a small plate

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve a spoonful with kanji, kappa, rice, dosa or puttu.
steps.visual: A mound of thenga chammanthi on a banana leaf beside a bowl of rice kanji, a roasted red chilli on top

substitutions.note: A few pieces of raw mango make the classic manga chammanthi.

recipes.title: Inji Curry (Sweet-Sour Ginger Tamarind Relish)
recipes.description: The dark, glossy sadya relish of ginger fried crisp in coconut oil and simmered in tamarind with jaggery and chilli — sweet, sour and hot. A little goes a long way.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Peel and finely chop the ginger. Squeeze the soaked tamarind and strain the liquid, adding the rest of the water.
steps.visual: Finely chopped ginger on a board beside a bowl of strained brown tamarind water

steps.title: Fry the ginger
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadai and fry the ginger on medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until golden brown and crisp. Lift out, leaving the oil.
steps.visual: Golden brown, crisp chopped ginger frying in coconut oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: In the same oil, splutter mustard seeds, then add fenugreek, dried red chillies, green chillies and curry leaves for 30 seconds. Add chilli powder, turmeric and hing and stir for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Mustard seeds, red and green chillies and curry leaves in reddened coconut oil in the kadai

steps.title: Simmer in tamarind
steps.text: Pour in the tamarind water, add the jaggery, salt and three-quarters of the fried ginger. Simmer on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until thick, dark and glossy like jam.
steps.visual: Thick, dark brown, glossy inji curry bubbling in the kadai with bits of ginger throughout

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stir in the remaining crisp ginger, cool and serve a teaspoon or two at a time with rice, curd rice or as part of a sadya.
steps.visual: A small spoonful of dark, glossy inji curry with crisp ginger bits on a banana leaf

substitutions.note: Use gluten-free hing or leave it out for a gluten-free relish.
Halve the jaggery for a sharper, less sweet relish.

recipes.storage: Keeps 2 weeks in a clean glass jar in the fridge.

recipes.title: Kumbalanga Curry (Ash Gourd in Coconut–Cumin Gravy)
recipes.description: Soft ash gourd simmered in a smooth coconut, cumin and green chilli gravy, finished with a shallot and red-chilli tempering. Light, mild and naturally low in carbs.

steps.title: Cook the ash gourd
steps.text: Cook the ash gourd cubes in a saucepan with turmeric, chilli powder, salt and the water, covered, on medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until translucent and soft.
steps.visual: Translucent pale ash gourd cubes simmering in yellow-orange water in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Grind the coconut
steps.text: Grind the coconut, cumin and green chillies with ½ cup water to a very smooth paste.
steps.visual: Smooth white coconut paste with green flecks in a mixer jar

steps.title: Simmer with coconut
steps.text: Add the paste to the ash gourd and simmer on low heat for 4 to 5 minutes until the gravy thickens slightly. Don't boil hard.
steps.visual: Ash gourd cubes in a creamy pale yellow coconut gravy in the saucepan

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil, splutter mustard seeds, add dried red chillies, shallots and curry leaves and fry until the shallots are golden. Pour over the curry.
steps.visual: Golden shallots, red chillies and curry leaves in coconut oil being poured over the pale yellow curry

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve with matta rice and a fish fry or thoran, or with cauliflower rice for a lighter plate.
steps.visual: Kumbalanga curry in a clay bowl, translucent ash gourd in creamy yellow gravy topped with fried shallots and curry leaves

substitutions.note: Chayote (chow chow) works the same way.

recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat.

recipes.title: Ragi Thenga Ada (Savoury Ragi–Coconut Flatbread)
recipes.description: Soft finger-millet flatbreads mixed with coconut, shallots, green chilli and cumin, pressed thin and cooked on a tawa — a quick Kerala breakfast with chammanthi or curry.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the ragi flour, coconut, shallots, green chilli, curry leaves, cumin and salt. Add warm water a little at a time and knead to a soft, slightly sticky dough. Rest 5 minutes.
steps.visual: A soft, dark brown ragi dough studded with white coconut, pink shallots and green chilli in a steel bowl

steps.title: Divide and press
steps.text: Divide into 8 balls. With wet fingers, pat each one out thinly on a greased banana leaf or a sheet of oiled parchment to about 5 inches across.
steps.visual: A thin round of ragi dough pressed out on a piece of banana leaf, wet fingertips marks visible, more dough balls waiting

steps.title: Cook on the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium heat and brush with coconut oil. Flip the ada onto the tawa (peel off the leaf after a minute) and cook for 2 minutes per side, with a few drops of oil, until firm with brown spots.
steps.visual: A dark brown ragi ada with coconut flecks and browned spots cooking on a black iron tawa

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot, two adas per person, with thenga chammanthi, egg roast or kadala curry.
steps.visual: Two round ragi adas with coconut and shallot flecks on a banana leaf beside a mound of red coconut chammanthi

substitutions.note: Jowar flour makes a lighter-coloured ada; use slightly more water.

recipes.storage: Best fresh; keep covered for a few hours.
recipes.reheating: Warm on a tawa for 30 seconds per side.

recipes.title: Ela Ada (Steamed Rice Parcels with Coconut and Jaggery)
recipes.description: Thin rice-flour dough spread on banana leaves, filled with coconut, cardamom and a modest amount of jaggery, folded and steamed. A traditional Kerala tea-time sweet made less sugary.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Melt the jaggery with 2 tablespoons of the water in a saucepan on low heat. Add the coconut and cardamom and stir for 4 to 5 minutes until the mixture is moist but no longer runny. Cool.
steps.visual: Golden-brown sticky coconut and jaggery filling in a steel saucepan

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Boil the remaining water with the salt and ghee. Pour it over the rice flour in a bowl, stirring with a spoon, then knead when cool enough into a soft, smooth dough that is softer than chapati dough.
steps.visual: A soft, smooth white rice-flour dough in a steel bowl

steps.title: Prepare banana leaves
steps.text: Cut banana leaves into 6 rectangles about 8 × 6 inches and wilt them briefly over a flame so they fold without cracking.
steps.visual: Six glossy rectangles of wilted green banana leaf stacked on the counter

steps.title: Spread and fill
steps.text: Place a lemon-sized ball of dough on each leaf and spread it thin with wet fingers. Put 2 tablespoons of filling on one half and fold the leaf over to close, pressing the edges.
steps.visual: A thin white layer of rice dough on a banana leaf with a line of brown coconut filling on one half, a folded parcel beside it

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the parcels in a steamer or idli pot for 12 to 15 minutes until the dough turns translucent and doesn't stick when touched.
steps.visual: Folded banana-leaf parcels stacked in a steamer, leaves darkened and steam rising

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm in the leaf with tea. One ada is a serving.
steps.visual: An opened banana-leaf parcel showing a translucent white rice ada with brown coconut-jaggery filling peeking through

substitutions.note: Chopped dates can sweeten the filling instead, though they are still sugar.
Ragi ela ada is a darker, higher-fibre version.

recipes.storage: Keeps 1 day at room temperature or 2 days refrigerated, wrapped in the leaf.
recipes.reheating: Re-steam for 3 to 4 minutes.
